chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ismail ibn Jabir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Book of God — in it is the news of what was before you, and information of what is to be after you, and the arbitration of what is between you, and we know it (all).

key_terms.خَبَرُ: Information, tidings — refers to eschatological and future events
key_terms.فَصْلُ: Arbitration, decisive judgment — the Quran as the criterion resolving disputes
key_terms.نَبَأُ: News, report — refers to historical narratives of past nations
key_terms.نَعْلَمُهُ: We know it — the Imam's claim to comprehensive knowledge of the Quran

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the comprehensiveness of the Quran?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) describes the Quran as a comprehensive guide encompassing past news, future information, and present judgments. The Imam's closing declaration — 'and we know it (all)' — is a profound assertion of the Ahl al-Bayt's special and complete knowledge of the Quran. This hadith was addressed to the companions of the Imam who sought to understand the authoritative source of Islamic guidance, emphasizing that the Quran's full meaning is known to the divinely-guided Imams.
